evidence: Single package ('ctcache') with multiple modules (clang_tidy_cache.py, clang_tidy_cache_server.py) indicating clear separation of concerns within one deployable unit

Clear logical layering: CLI/client entry point (clang_tidy_cache.py), server backend (clang_tidy_cache_server.py), and tooling scripts (tools/, doc/latex/tools/) — but no inter-process communication or network boundaries
High fan-out (avg 8.11) reflects internal module interdependencies typical of a monolithic design where modules depend on shared utilities and domain logic
Shared data models (e.g., ClangTidyCacheOpts, cache interfaces) and dependency injection via class composition across core modules
Tooling scripts reuse common modules (e.g., doc/latex/tools/* imports from common.py), indicating internal modularity without separation into services
Deployed as a unified artifact (Dockerfile, systemd services) with no indication of distributed components
risks: Tight coupling between server and client logic could hinder maintainability as project scales
Monolithic deployment model limits independent scaling and fault isolation
Shared state in multi-cache and stats modules may introduce concurrency issues under load
